final_qi.long_answer: Research into Absent tibia‐polydactyly‐arachnoid cyst syndrome evaluated whether mutations in a gene located on chromosome 2 might be responsible for the condition. The gene studied was the Indian hedgehog (IHH) gene, which is known to be important in skeletal development. Analysis of patients with the syndrome revealed that no abnormalities were present in the IHH gene, thus excluding it as the cause of the syndrome.

The gene studied was the Indian hedgehog (IHH) gene, which is known to be important in skeletal development. candidate.long_answer: Studies that investigated the genetic basis of Absent tibia-polydactyly-arachnoid cyst syndrome examined the HOXD13 gene, which is found in the HOXD gene cluster on chromosome 2. However, the investigations revealed that HOXD13 did not carry any abnormalities in affected patients, leading to the conclusion that mutations in this gene are not responsible for the syndrome.
